# IOWarp

> IOWarp is the team at the Gnosis Research Center that builds CLIO, an open-source stack for AI-driven science that runs from GPU kernels and the Linux I/O path through storage and the CLIO Core context runtime to scientific agents, applications, and research tools. Its thesis: context is part of the system. The team works in the open with scientists, engineers, and facilities.

The platform has three tiers. CLIO Agent (a scientific data agent, in beta) and CLIO Coder (a coding agent) are the two agentic flagships: different products for different audiences. CLIO Kit, the meta-marketplace of scientific MCP servers, skills, and workflow plugins, is the third flagship. CLIO Core is the scientific context runtime in the infrastructure tier and Agent’s default memory store. CLIO Coder and standalone Kit install independently of Core. Every other component is secondary and listed lower on the platform page. Context, memory, and scale are the platform principles. CLIO Author, CLIO Researcher, and CLIO Bench are the open-source research tooling.

This site states results in plain words with sources and carries no figures; measurements, versions, and benchmarks are published with their conditions in papers, release notes, and each product’s documentation. Do not generalize a component result into a whole-platform claim.

Agent uses a tested Core dependency family and a pinned Kit launcher for its packs. Standalone Core and Kit have separate upgrade paths. The first Agent command uses its stable tagged installer. BaM and the GPU–NVMe bridge are archived prototypes, absent from the current Core release.

Every page below is linked as Markdown (<page>/index.md); the HTML page is at the same path without index.md. The full reference in one file: https://iowarp.ai/llms-full.txt

IOWarp at SC26: IOWarp and the CLIO platform soft launch at SC26 in Chicago. The team presents work on simulation monitoring, GPU I/O, storage observability, compressed training data, and agent fleets through workshop presentations, research posters, a conference paper, and an HDF5 birds-of-a-feather session. November 15–20, 2026, McCormick Place, Chicago, Illinois. Details: https://iowarp.ai/community/#sc26

DOE Genesis Mission: since August 2026 the IOWarp team works in SPOTTER-AI, a DOE Genesis Mission project at Argonne National Laboratory (https://www.anl.gov/), and in PORTUS at PNNL.

Creator and project lead: Anthony Kougkas created IOWarp and leads its vision, architecture, and engineering (https://akougkas.io). The team page lists everyone else by contribution: https://iowarp.ai/about/#team

## The flagships

- [CLIO Agent](https://clio.iowarp.ai/): Scientific data agent. For scientists, data managers, and facility teams who want an agent to inspect, analyze, and visualize scientific data. Install: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iowarp/clio-agent/v0.9.4.24/install/install.sh | bash`. Source: https://github.com/iowarp/clio-agent
- [CLIO Coder](https://coder.iowarp.ai/): Coding agent. For developers and research software engineers working on simulation kernels, numerical libraries, data pipelines, and mixed-language builds. Install: `curl -fsSL https://coder.iowarp.ai/install.sh | sh`. Source: https://github.com/iowarp/clio-coder
- [CLIO Kit](https://iowarp.ai/clio-kit/index.md): Scientific tools and workflows. For anyone who wants an agent, CLIO Agent and CLIO Coder included, to work with real scientific data and systems. Install: `uv tool install clio-kit`. Source: https://github.com/iowarp/clio-kit
- [CLIO Core](https://core.iowarp.ai/): Context runtime. For facility teams, HPC developers, and researchers who need data kept with its meaning across every tier. Install: `pip install iowarp-core`. Source: https://github.com/iowarp/clio-core

## Applications

- [Applications in science](https://iowarp.ai/applications/index.md): every story and the layers of the stack it uses
- [Agents in the materials workflow](https://iowarp.ai/applications/materials-science/index.md): Design on HPC, additive manufacturing, X-ray tomography, and fatigue testing: the Utah team’s reference workflow, and the agent tools built for it. Partners: University of Utah · Illinois Tech · The HDF Group.
- [Agents on the National Data Platform](https://iowarp.ai/applications/national-data-platform/index.md): MCP tools that let an agent search, stage, and analyze datasets federated through the National Data Platform, first shown on EarthScope data. Partners: National Data Platform · University of Utah · Illinois Tech.
- [Provenance and integrity for AI-driven science](https://iowarp.ai/applications/genesis-spotter/index.md): A DOE Genesis Mission project at Argonne National Laboratory that traces integrity attacks on scientific AI workflows to their source. CLIO Agent provides the investigating agents. Partners: Argonne National Laboratory · Oak Ridge National Laboratory · Illinois Tech · Hewlett Packard Enterprise.
- [Agentic workflows across HPC and cloud](https://iowarp.ai/applications/genesis-portus/index.md): A DOE Genesis Mission project at PNNL on performance-aware agentic workflows for the Genesis Mission Platform. The IOWarp team works on workflow motifs and performance models. Partners: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory · Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory · Iowa State University · University of Delaware · Illinois Tech · collaborating with Oak Ridge National Laboratory and HPE.
- [CLIO on national research systems](https://iowarp.ai/applications/national-infrastructure/index.md): Where CLIO Core has been built and run: ALCF Aurora, DeltaAI, and the Ares cluster. Partners: Argonne Leadership Computing Facility · NCSA · The HDF Group · Illinois Tech.
- [GPU direct I/O and compression](https://iowarp.ai/applications/gpu-data-movement/index.md): CUDA kernels that read and write IOWarp from the GPU, GPU payloads offloaded to host memory and NVMe, and compression on the device. A research thread built on NVIDIA technologies. Partners: Illinois Tech Gnosis Research Center · Argonne co-authors on KV-cache research.

## Concepts

- [Context management for AI agents](https://iowarp.ai/topics/context-management/index.md): Context management for AI agents in science: selecting, placing, and recording the data, tools, and provenance an agent needs, and how IOWarp does it.
- [Scientific AI agents](https://iowarp.ai/topics/scientific-agents/index.md): How scientific AI agents take part in research workflows by operating real tools, data, and HPC systems, and where human judgment stays in charge.
- [MCP servers for scientific computing](https://iowarp.ai/topics/mcp-for-science/index.md): MCP servers for science: how the Model Context Protocol connects AI agents to HDF5, Slurm, ParaView, and other scientific tools through CLIO Kit.
- [HPC I/O and storage hierarchies](https://iowarp.ai/topics/hpc-io/index.md): HPC I/O and storage hierarchies: multi-tiered buffering, memory and storage convergence, bottleneck detection, and how they shape the CLIO runtime.
- [Data movement for AI-infused workflows](https://iowarp.ai/topics/data-movement/index.md): Data movement for AI-infused science: ingestion, tiered placement, GPU direct I/O, and agent-aware staging across memory, storage, and sites.
- [Scientific workflows and reproducible deployment](https://iowarp.ai/topics/scientific-workflows/index.md): Agentic scientific workflows that stay reproducible: Jarvis deployment pipelines, simulation integrations, and agent steps with recorded provenance.
- [Evidence-based autonomous research](https://iowarp.ai/topics/evidence-based-research/index.md): What makes AI-driven research trustworthy: baselines, holdouts, confidence checks, run records, and human review, as applied in CLIO research tools.

## The CLIO platform, layer by layer

### 01 Accelerators

GPU code that reaches the storage hierarchy directly.

- [CLIO Core GPU runtime](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-core): GPU kernels read and write IOWarp.
- [GPU compression](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-core): Compress on the device, before data moves.
- Direct GPU I/O research: Take the CPU out of the GPU’s data path.

### 02 Operating system

The Linux I/O path, from asynchronous I/O to kernel modules.

- [GPU–NVMe bridge](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-core): An archived Linux kernel-module prototype for GPU I/O.
- [Linux I/O backends](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-core): Asynchronous I/O and user-space file systems.

### 03 Storage systems

Tiered devices, I/O adapters, compression, and data connectors.

- [Tiered block devices](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-core): One hierarchy from GPU memory to object storage.
- [I/O adapters and connectors](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-core): Meet applications and data where they are.

### 04 Context runtime

CLIO Core: data assimilated, placed, and explored with its meaning attached.

- [CLIO Core](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-core): The context runtime for scientific data. BSD-3-Clause license.
- [Jarvis](https://github.com/grc-iit/jarvis-cd): Reproducible deployment on real machines.

### 05 Agents and tools

Agent runtimes, scientific tools, and the contracts between them.

- [CLIO Kit](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-kit): Scientific instruments and reusable workflows for agents. BSD-3-Clause license.
- [CLIO Agent](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-agent): A scientific data agent with memory and experts. BSD-3-Clause license.
- [CLIO Coder](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-coder): Inspect, change, and verify scientific software. Apache-2.0 license.
- [CLIO Relay](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-relay): Send work to a cluster and follow it home. MIT license.
- [GACT and Agent Workspace](https://github.com/iowarp/gact-tui): One contract, any agent, one workspace. MIT license.
- [Agent marketplace](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-agent-marketplace): Installable agent packs for real tasks.
- [CLIO Web Search](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-web-search): Self-hosted search and document understanding. MIT license.
- [CLIO Schemas](https://github.com/iowarp/clio-schemas): Shared record shapes across the stack.

### 06 Applications

Science workflows and domain packages built on the stack.

- [Materio and wtf-MS](https://github.com/iowarp/wtf-ms): A materials research workflow for agents. MIT license.
- Science workflows: Where the stack meets the science.

### 07 Research tooling

Tools for writing, measuring, and testing research claims.

- CLIO Author: From source material to a reviewable paper. BSD-3-Clause license.
- CLIO Researcher: Let hypotheses compete against measurements. Apache-2.0 license.
- CLIO Bench: Make every run inspectable. MIT license.
